statement: Three of the 12 corners of a regular 12-sided polygon are chosen and joined to make a triangle. For how many of these triangles is at least one side also a side of the polygon?

choices.misconception: I counted 10 triangles on each of the 12 sides of the polygon, $12 \times 10$, without noticing that a triangle using two sides of the polygon was counted twice.
I saw that the 12 triangles using two sides of the polygon were counted twice, but I took away both counts, $120 - 24$, so those triangles were not counted at all.
I counted every triangle, $\binom{12}{3} = 220$, without checking that at least one side lies along the polygon.
I divided 120 by 3, thinking every triangle was counted once for each of its sides, but most of these triangles have only one side on the polygon.

hints: Count by the side of the polygon that the triangle uses.
Each side of the polygon, together with any third corner, makes a triangle. Then ask which triangles use two sides of the polygon, and how many times they were counted.
Each of the 12 sides goes with 10 third corners: $12 \times 10 = 120$ counts. A triangle made of three neighbouring corners uses two sides, so it was counted twice; there are 12 of them.

solutions.reliable: For each of the 12 sides of the polygon, any of the other 10 corners completes a triangle, giving $12 \times 10 = 120$ counts. A triangle with exactly one side on the polygon is counted once. A triangle with two sides on the polygon is made of three neighbouring corners, and it is counted twice, once for each of those sides; there are 12 such triangles, one for each middle corner. No triangle uses three sides, because the polygon has more than 3 sides. Removing the extra count for each of the 12 gives $120 - 12 = 108$. The transferable idea: when you count by a feature that some objects have more than once, find exactly how many times each was counted and correct for that.
solutions.elegant: Sort the triangles by how many polygon sides they use. Two sides: three neighbouring corners, 12 triangles. Exactly one side: a side together with a third corner that is not next to either of its ends, $12 \times 8 = 96$ triangles. In total $96 + 12 = 108$.

whyOnTest: Counting by sides is quick, and the 5-point step is spotting which triangles were counted twice and correcting by exactly that much.
